question: Which of the following is the best example of a heterogeneous mixture?

options.text: Mixture of iron chloride and iron fillings

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mixture of iron chloride and iron fillings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A heterogeneous mixture is one in which the components can be visibly distinguished and are not uniformly distributed.
 
• The mixture of iron chloride and iron fillings is an example of a heterogeneous mixture because the two substances remain distinct and separate.
 
• In this mixture, iron fillings can be seen as solid particles distinct from the iron chloride.
 
• Such mixtures do not have a uniform composition throughout and the different components can be easily separated by physical methods like filtration or magnetic separation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Homogeneous Mixture:**

 
 
• It is a mixture in which the composition is uniform throughout.
 
• Examples include solutions like salt in water or sugar in water where the solute is completely dissolved.
 
• Homogeneous mixtures cannot be separated by simple physical methods.
 
 
 
• **Methods of Separation:**
 
 
• **Filtration:** Used to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid.
 
• **Magnetic Separation:** Useful for separating magnetic materials from non-magnetic ones.
 
• **Evaporation:** Used to separate a dissolved solid from a liquid by evaporating the liquid.
 
 
 
• **Colloids:**
 
 
• A type of homogeneous mixture where the particle size is intermediate between a true solution and a suspension.
 
• Examples include milk, fog, and jelly.
 
 
 
• **Suspensions:**
 
 
• A type of heterogeneous mixture where the particles are large enough to settle out over time.
 
• Examples include sand in water or dust in air.
